# Detectability of the staged experiment (report §6)

*Generated by `scripts/phase1/21_quant_checks.py power`. Pure arithmetic, no network, re-run by `run.sh`. Every input is an **assumption**, not a measurement from this child's cells — see the assumption list below.*

Two-proportion two-sided test, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80. Counting unit is one scored division (Stage C) or one scored cell (Stage D). `cultures/arm` assumes **100** units scored per culture and inflates by the design effect `1 + (m-1)·ICC` for clustering of units within a culture.

| Endpoint | baseline | relative reduction | treated | units/arm | cultures/arm ICC=0 | ICC=0.01 | ICC=0.05 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stage C — missegregation events per division | 0.10 | one third | 0.07 | 1,081 | 11 | 22 | 65 |
| Stage C — missegregation events per division | 0.10 | one half | 0.05 | 435 | 5 | 9 | 26 |
| Stage C — missegregation events per division | 0.20 | one third | 0.13 | 489 | 5 | 10 | 30 |
| Stage C — missegregation events per division | 0.20 | one half | 0.10 | 199 | 2 | 4 | 12 |
| Stage C — missegregation events per division | 0.30 | one third | 0.20 | 294 | 3 | 6 | 18 |
| Stage C — missegregation events per division | 0.30 | one half | 0.15 | 121 | 2 | 3 | 8 |
| Stage D — aneuploid fraction of the surviving population | 0.20 | one third | 0.13 | 489 | 5 | 10 | 30 |
| Stage D — aneuploid fraction of the surviving population | 0.20 | one half | 0.10 | 199 | 2 | 4 | 12 |
| Stage D — aneuploid fraction of the surviving population | 0.30 | one third | 0.20 | 294 | 3 | 6 | 18 |
| Stage D — aneuploid fraction of the surviving population | 0.30 | one half | 0.15 | 121 | 2 | 3 | 8 |
| Stage D — aneuploid fraction of the surviving population | 0.40 | one third | 0.27 | 196 | 2 | 4 | 12 |
| Stage D — aneuploid fraction of the surviving population | 0.40 | one half | 0.20 | 82 | 1 | 2 | 5 |

**The reference design.** Stage D at a baseline aneuploid fraction of 0.30 and a one-third relative reduction (0.30 -> 0.20) needs **294 scored cells per arm**. At 100 cells per culture that is **3 cultures per arm** if units within a culture are independent, and **18 cultures per arm** at ICC = 0.05. The design rule stated in §6 (≥ 3 independent biological replicates) therefore covers the replicate *structure* and not the *power*: three cultures per arm suffice only for a large effect with near-zero between-culture variance.

**What each number assumes, and what would replace it.**

- *Baseline rate.* Unmeasured in this child's cells. Stage C's first run is what replaces it; until then the row to read is a range, not a point.
- *Effect size.* No NAD+-raising agent has been tested in this disease or this allele class, so the one-third / one-half columns are scenario values chosen to bracket a plausible rescue, not predictions. If the true effect is smaller than a third, every number here is an underestimate.
- *ICC.* Between-culture clustering has not been measured for these endpoints. ICC = 0.05 with 100 units per culture already multiplies the requirement by 5.95, which is why the column exists rather than a single headline n.
- *One-sided vs two-sided.* Two-sided throughout, because a rise in the aneuploid fraction is a result this experiment must be able to detect (§6 Stage D).
- *What this is not.* A power calculation is not evidence that the effect exists. It states what the proposed experiment could see if it did.
